title: Veterans Day, 2025
summary:
This proclamation marks Veterans Day 2025, honoring the service and sacrifice of those who have worn the uniform, and formally setting November 11 as the national day to recognize them. It also highlights actions the administration says it has taken to improve support for veterans and calls on Americans and public officials to take part in ceremonies and display the flag.

The document points to changes at the Department of Veterans Affairs, including new health clinics, faster access to benefits, and steps to make it easier for survivors to receive what they are due. It says the backlog of claims has been reduced and that a new National Center for Warrior Independence will provide housing for up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028. It also notes policy reversals that end diversity, equity, and inclusion programs and transgender-related policies within veteran services, with the stated aim of directing more funds to immediate needs. In addition, it references new tax measures that make earlier tax cuts permanent and remove taxes on Social Security for most seniors, which the proclamation says will ease pressure on veterans living on fixed incomes.

Those who are likely to benefit include veterans seeking faster health care and disability decisions, veterans experiencing homelessness who may gain access to housing, surviving family members who depend on earned benefits, and seniors who may see lower tax bills. Communities near the new clinics and those participating in Veterans Day events may also feel a positive impact.

Those who might be negatively affected include veterans and staff who value diversity and inclusion initiatives or who rely on transgender-specific policies, as the rollback may reduce targeted support. People concerned about the long-term cost of making past tax cuts permanent and reducing Social Security tax revenue may worry about future funding for public services, including veteran programs. Others may question the scale or pace of the improvements described.

Overall, the proclamation asks the country to honor veterans with gratitude while emphasizing a policy agenda the administration says is meant to deliver more direct care, housing, and financial relief.
